name: Foldseek
compares: Predicted 3-D shapes. Each residue of an AlphaFold model gets one of 20 shape letters (3Di) from its local fold. The shape letters are aligned together with the amino acids.
reference: AlphaFold models of the relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04 accessions), as a Foldseek database.
score: Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
failure_modes: A protein with no AlphaFold model cannot be searched. Five relatives have no Foldseek rows at all (chimpanzee, cow, dog, opossum, western clawed frog): not run.

AlphaFold models of long proteins come in overlapping pieces (F1, F2, ...). The task script moves piece n's coordinates 200 x (n - 1) residues along the protein; if a piece started elsewhere, its calls would land in the wrong place. Checked against the real piece starts: not measured.
command:
foldseek search \
    human-38fdd87d_fsdb/db zebrafish_fsdb/db result foldseek_tmp \
    --threads 16 \
    -e 10.0 \
    --max-seqs 1000

cost_per_1000_queries.hardware: Stanford Sherlock, SLURM partition hns; searches on CPU only

questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.164 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.241 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.268 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.167 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting `3di_aa`; strata with at least 30 true instances.)
Do you have an AlphaFold model for every protein you want to annotate? If not, Foldseek cannot search the proteins without one.
Can you spend about 0.133 CPU-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured cost against zebrafish; the range over relatives is under "Cost per 1,000 queries" above.
